rows.finding: Numerator is 0.82*(Ec*tf/(eta*Ef*tc))^(1/2)*(eta*Ef); denominator is 1+0.64*Kdelta. Equation 2.2-13 defines Kdelta=delta*Ec/(tc*Fc).
Fc is the lowest flatwise core compression, core tension, and core-to-facing bond strength. Stabilized compression is only one candidate.

rows.location: Table II, 3/8 inch, 1.0 pcf; PDF p. 5
rows.finding: Bare compression 55 psi typical / 25 psi minimum average; stabilized 60 / 35 psi; compression modulus 15 ksi typical; crush strength 35 psi typical. Tests at 0.625 inch. The min column means minimum average for a product type.

rows.location: printed p. 2-33, Eqs. 2.2-15/16; rationale at p. 2-26
rows.finding: Wrinkling interaction Rx^3+Ry=1 uses separately normalized uniaxial critical loads. Equal critical loads and equal applied compression yield the scalar cubic. The earlier rationale is large-aspect-ratio flat plates.

Intracell uniaxial coefficient K=2 uses cell size across flats. Its biaxial interaction is Rx+Ry=1, giving one half for equal compression. The text says sufficiently large dimples can precipitate wrinkling; separate scalar margins are not proof of independence.

0.33 is selected from test data, not a measured wave. The test subset excludes poor bonds with flatwise tension below compression and uses cases close to elastic behavior. Final matching-configuration tests are recommended.

Norris, Boller and Voss. Cell size affects wrinkling wavelength; fitted wavelength is not necessarily equal to cell size. Original-wave scaling assumptions differ between continuous and honeycomb cores.

rows.location: Part I introduction, printed p. 2; authors cross-checked against CR-1457 ref. 2-9
rows.finding: Fourier components near the critical wavelength are amplified; neighboring wavelengths can also contribute. Complete cited author list: Norris, Ericksen, March, Smith and Boller. March, not Kommers, is the third author.

rows.finding: Larger cells with thin skins may telegraph into a dimpled surface; no numerical depth or qualified Be-bonded waveform tolerance is supplied.

Flatness is ±0.008 inch per radial foot. Selected stock variants have 0.040 inch faces, 3003 aluminum core and 5052-H32 faces. A separate 0.125 inch panel variant uses 0.020 inch faces. These are panel tolerances, not critical-mode amplitude measurements.
Balanced aluminum panels: ±0.7 mm per radial metre, conditional on panel construction and fixturing.
Wave ±1 mm and overall ±1/16 inch (printed parenthetic 1.5 mm) per 60 inch. The parenthetic metric number is a rounded manufacturer statement, not an exact inch conversion.

Finished welded metallic core within 0.010 inch under hold-down of no more than 7 psi; local steps no more than 0.003 inch. Scope lists titanium, nickel alloys and stainless steel, not this bonded aluminum/Be sandwich.

Official H record confirms hot-rolled Be sheet/plate and the nominal thickness scope, but the retrieved public page does not expose §3.5.5 or quantitative flatness classes. This check cannot confirm the owner's three-class statement from primary text.
